newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran troops regain control of jail after riot.
newsitem.headline: Honduran troops regain control of jail after riot.

text.p: Troops regained control of a jail in southern Honduras on Thursday after 500 rioting inmates ended a stand-off that left seven people wounded, officials said.
Five prisoners and two guards were injured in an exchange of gunfire early on Thursday, but officials said the rioting inmates laid down their guns after authorities talked to them.
"The situation has been neutralised, and the prisoners gave up after we talked them out of using further violence," Lt. Norman Padilla told reporters.

The riot broke out during a power cut late on Wednesday, when prisoners seized control of sections of the jail, located in the city of Choluteca, 70 miles (110 km) south of the capital. During the riot, prisoners engaged in prolonged exchanges of gunfire with troops and set one of the offices on fire.
Police and army troops captured 30 prisoners who tried to escape. They surrounded the jail to prevent a mass breakout.
